title: Reading Makes Me Happy Now
author: Amy Coombe
summary: At the end of an academic year, a reading lead reflects on the transformation that effective reading instruction can produce in students. Students who have struggled with reading for years rarely see themselves as readers, and these negative self-perceptions become deeply embedded, affecting confidence, behavior, and long-term life chances. Effective intervention does more than improve literacy skills; it rewrites the story students tell themselves about who they are. Student testimonials gathered at year-end show a dramatic shift from shame and avoidance to confidence and pride in reading aloud. The author argues that teaching reading is the most important job educators have because it changes not just literacy ability, but children's fundamental beliefs about what they are capable of becoming.
points: Students who struggle with reading develop deeply embedded negative self-perceptions that influence their confidence, behaviour, attention, future life chances, and participation in society.
Effective reading instruction changes not only students' literacy skills but also the story they tell themselves about who they are and what they are capable of becoming.
Student testimonials demonstrate that children once reluctant to read aloud become eager to volunteer, proud to read for visitors, and describe their reading lessons as fun.
Reading-age data is a valuable marker of progress, but just as meaningful — sometimes more so — is the shift in students' beliefs about themselves as readers.
Teaching children to read is the most important job educators have, because it changes how students see themselves and what they believe they are capable of becoming.
quotes: Students who’ve struggled with reading for years almost never see themselves as readers. They don’t enjoy reading. They often don’t enjoy school, unsurprisingly, given how much classroom learning relies on an ability to read well.

Unless we intervene, these self perceptions become deeply embedded, influencing their self-confidence, behaviour, attention, future life chances, choices, participation in society, relationships and parenting.
the most effective way to do so is to teach them how to read, believe that they can, and guarantee that they experience success. When we do so, we begin to rewrite the story they tell themselves.
Please can you ask me to read when visitors come into our reading lessons because I can read aloud really well now and I want people to see.
I can’t believe how much better my reading is than this time last year. I can read such big words now, and this really helps me in other subjects, like Science!
Reading-age data is a valuable marker of progress, but just as meaningful is students’ beliefs about themselves.

When we teach children to read, we don’t just change their reading knowledge. We change the way they see themselves and what they believe they are capable of becoming. This is why teaching our children to read is our most important job.
